body:
Fixes #5987.

With `JSON_DIAGNOSTICS` and `JSON_DIAGNOSTIC_POSITIONS` both set, an exception about the **root** value lost its `(bytes a-b)` range, because `exception::diagnostics()` returned early when the path had no tokens, before the byte range was appended. The json_view `diagnostics()` copied the same early return.

### Changes

- `detail/exceptions.hpp` and `detail/view/errors.hpp`: build the `(path) ` prefix only if there are tokens; always append the byte range.
- `detail/exceptions.hpp`: `get_byte_positions()` returns no range for a null value. Without the early return, a value-initialized iterator (`json::iterator{} == j.begin()`, `invalid_iterator.212`) would now reach it with `JSON_DIAGNOSTICS` set too and dereference the null pointer. This is the same change and test as #6003, so the two PRs can be merged in either order.
- `detail/view/errors.hpp`: the `found` result of `value_path()` is no longer needed. A value that is not found leaves no tokens, just like the root.
- Tests: root, nested and constructed values in `unit-diagnostic-positions.cpp` (runs with and without `JSON_DIAGNOSTICS`) and `unit-json_view_positions.cpp`; the value-initialized iterator comparison from #6003 in `unit-diagnostic-positions.cpp`. One existing json_view check encoded the old behaviour ("no bytes for the root with `JSON_DIAGNOSTICS`") and now expects the range.
- Docs: `json_diagnostic_positions.md` states that the root value also gets its range.

| build | root | nested |
|---|---|---|
| `JSON_DIAGNOSTICS` only | — | `(/1) ` |
| `JSON_DIAGNOSTIC_POSITIONS` only | `(bytes 0-4) ` | `(bytes 4-8) ` |
| both (before) | — | `(/1) (bytes 4-8) ` |
| both (after) | `(bytes 0-4) ` | `(/1) (bytes 4-8) ` |

A value without positions (constructed, not parsed) still gets no range and no stray whitespace.

### Performance

Only the exception-message path changes (it runs after a throw), so successful operations are unaffected.

### Public API

No breaking changes. The `what()` text of exceptions about the root value changes in builds with both macros set: it now contains the byte range, as it already did with `JSON_DIAGNOSTIC_POSITIONS` alone. Since 3.12.0.

### Verification

Both test files fail on develop with `JSON_DIAGNOSTICS=1` and pass with the fix; full `ctest` with ASan+UBSan: 188/188.

### Performance check

**No performance impact.** The change only affects how the context string of an exception is built, which runs only after something has already gone wrong.

- **Generated code** (default configuration): all 1,052 functions of the benchmark binary are byte-for-byte identical between base and PR. The changed code in `exceptions.hpp` and `view/errors.hpp` exists only under `JSON_DIAGNOSTICS`/`JSON_DIAGNOSTIC_POSITIONS`. Even there it runs only while an exception is being constructed (`diagnostics()` is instantiated only at throw sites), so no non-throwing path changes.
- **Instruction counts**: all 38 rows are within ±0.4 %, as expected for identical code (e.g. parse twitter 1.0003, `json_document` parse twitter 1.0004).

<details><summary>Method</summary>

- PR head vs. its base (merge base), both compiled into one binary (namespaces renamed per copy) with the same workload: DOM parse (string, stream, callback), copy/destroy, `==`/`<`, iteration, `dump()`, msgpack/UBJSON/BJData read and write, `json_document` parse/`dump()`/`==`/`get<std::int64_t>()` on twitter, citm_catalog, canada and small_signed_ints.
- **Generated code**: both variants disassembled (Apple clang 21, `-O3`, arm64), names and addresses masked, compared function by function.
- **Instruction counts**: Apple M1 Max, instructions retired per repetition (minimum of 3 runs, setup subtracted). Rows whose machine code is identical vary by about ±0.4 %, which is the noise floor. Where a hot path changes, also GCC 13.3 `-O3` on x86-64 under callgrind, which gives exact counts (built with `-falign-functions=64 -falign-loops=64` unless a row says otherwise).
</details>

*Written by Claude Code on behalf of @nlohmann.*

**AppVeyor** (`continuous-integration/appveyor/pr`) fails on ae792a4. This does not appear to be caused by this PR:

- The AppVeyor branch build of `develop` itself fails as well (status from 02:17 UTC today), before this PR's build ran.
- This PR only changes how the exception context string is built under `JSON_DIAGNOSTICS`/`JSON_DIAGNOSTIC_POSITIONS`; all 168 GitHub Actions checks on this head pass, including the MSVC, clang-cl and MinGW jobs.

I could not read the AppVeyor log or re-run the build from here, so the root cause on `develop` is still open and no fix exists yet.
